A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

long‐range excitatory connections within olfactory cortical circuits are organized in a hierarchical manner, with bottom‐up (rostral–caud) excitatory connections accompanied by feedforward inhibitory connections, whereas top‐down (caudal–rostral) connections are weak and lack layer specificity.

the LRMGP is a hierarchical network with a bottom‐up feedforward excitation and a top‐down feedback inhibition, and the intercortical projections from the aPC to LEC and pPC to LEC are convergent and feedforward.
